name: shaded_blades
description: broad curved blades and petals on near-black, each a solid copper, slate, maroon or cream sheet shaded edge to edge like brushed metal, overlapping in fans that meet at small spiky stars of the same blades in miniature, the finest detail left dark with a hair of light along the set

reference.made_with: Ultra Fractal by its look (orbit-trap blades shaded by a gradient, signed exoteric.roach.org), 2560x1600

reuses: the bubble trap's lattice, entry step and largest (bronze_packing, ribbon_packing) with ribbon_packing's face (shift [0.5, 0.2]) and its crescent read: discs of radius 0.45 every 1, each entry's lune a blade, no larger than 0.3 frames and none smaller than 0.006 (smallest). This is the lune_blades formulation, Matt's one keep and the default since item 025; the strip shape this style added is not in the default stack
the palette layer by rank on the entry step at three cycles, masked to the lune: one flat colour per blade, neighbouring blades on different stops of a map whose hues alternate
the light layer at one band, rings 1, on the crescent read: each blade a band lit from one edge to the other, the brushed-metal sheen
a glow on the crescent, inverted, painted near-black: each blade darkening into its inner edge against the face, so overlapping blades separate
glow_filaments' hair glow (falloff 2e-4) on de, under the blades: the set's filigree in the dark the smallest bound leaves
the tone pass, at the reference's median and p10
adds: bubble member shape (disc | strip): the strip |Im((z - center) e^(-i tilt))| < radius, the line trap read at an entry; with spacing it repeats as parallel lines. Its pullbacks are crosses of tapering arms through each critical point of the iterate, so its entries are pointed blades; it has no face and no angle read
bubble member tilt (degrees): the strip's direction, and the axis the across read is measured across

bubble read across: (v / radius + 1) / 2, v the entry's offset across the tilt, 0 at one edge and 1 at the other, with its own gradient (the axis pulled back through conj(dz)) so a light shades every blade edge to edge
bubble member smallest (a fraction of the frame width): the read ends, NaN, at the first counted entry pulling back smaller than that, so the trap's detail stops there and the layers beneath show

knobs.name: blade_size
knobs.label: Blade size
knobs.what: the largest lune blade, as a share of the frame width; never larger than kept, or big blades hide the fine ones

knobs.name: fine_detail
knobs.label: Finest blade
knobs.what: the smallest blade drawn, as a share of the frame width; below it the set's own filigree shows

knobs.name: light_angle
knobs.label: Light direction
knobs.what: where the light comes from, in degrees round the frame (135 is the upper left)

knobs.name: sheen
knobs.label: Metal sheen
knobs.what: the brushed-metal highlight across each blade

notes: Added: the bubble trap's `strip` shape (`shape`, `tilt`), the `across` read and the `smallest` bound. Its default stack is the `lune_blades` formulation (crescent lunes, not strips), Matt's one keep

Lessons: The tenth style is broad shaded blades in copper, slate and cream on near-black, meeting at small spiky stars, and it went in as **one new shape of the bubble trap and two members**: the strip about a line (`shape`, `tilt`), the `across` read and the `smallest` bound. Everything else is old: a rank palette on the entry step at three cycles gives each blade one flat colour, in the strip formulation a light at one band and `rings` 1 on `across` made it a lit cylinder and an inverted glow on the height darkened its edges, where the default stack lights and darkens the crescent read instead; a falloff hair glow on `de` and a dim rank palette on the smooth count lie in the gaps beneath. Three lessons. **The shape of a trap is the shape of what it draws**: a disc's entries pull back round, so its crescents read as eyes, while a strip pulls back through each critical point as a cross of tapering arms, so a strip's entries are blades and the small ones crowding a critical point are spiky stars, the reference's ornaments, with no layer of their own. **An entry trap needs both bounds**: `largest` alone at 3 frames gives one blade filling the frame, at 0.3 a fan of them; with no lower bound the blades shrink into the set as hatching (striped fans of sub-pixel blades), and `smallest` 0.006 is what leaves the near-black gaps the reference is a fifth made of. **A dark reference's black share is held in the gaps, not by the ground's colour**: the tone pass carries p10 to 0.029 whatever the ground is, so a flat ground in a third of the frame reads black 0.30 against 0.22; a dim rank palette on the smooth count at 0.35 under the blades gives the gaps a gradient and the frame back its share. Its locations are an ordinary gallery scout (`--max-ink 0.12`); 32 of the 40 drafts hold the reference's balance, the misses frames flooded by one cream blade (p90) or by gap (black).
